[Step 07] Break the song into short sections. First listen to the section, then practice its notes or chord shapes slowly. Repeat each section until you can play it several times without stopping, then join it to the next section.

[Step 08] Practice changing between the song’s notes or chords. Move between just two at first, keeping a steady beat. If the change is difficult, slow down, simplify the rhythm, and prioritize clean sounds over speed.

[Step 09] Use a metronome or backing track once you can play the notes reliably. Start well below the song’s normal speed and increase the tempo a little only after you can play the section accurately several times.

[Step 10] Experiment with making a short melody. Choose a small set of notes that sound pleasant together, play them in different orders, and record the results. Try changing the rhythm or ending on a different note.

[Step 11] Follow a repeatable practice routine: spend a few minutes warming up, review a skill you already know, work on one difficult section, then play something for fun. Practice for 10–20 minutes on most days, and stop if you feel pain.

[Step 12] Keep track of what you practiced and what still feels difficult. Record yourself once a week, compare it with earlier recordings, and choose one specific target for the next week, such as smoother chord changes or steadier timing.

[Step 13] After you can play the first song comfortably, learn another song using one new skill at a time. Revisit earlier songs regularly so you can hear your progress and build a small repertoire."}
